raw.markdown:
# Sacroplasty — Authorization Guide

## CPT Codes — Sacroplasty

| CPT | Description |
| --- | --- |
| 0200T | Percutaneous sacral augmentation (sacroplasty), unilateral injection(s), including the use of a balloon or mechanical device, when used, 1 or more needles |
| 0201T | Percutaneous sacral augmentation (sacroplasty), bilateral injections, including the use of a balloon or mechanical device, when used, 2 or more needles |
| 72291 | Radiological supervision and interpretation, percutaneous vertebroplasty or vertebral augmentation; under fluoroscopic guidance |
| 72292 | Radiological supervision and interpretation; under CT guidance |

Note: CPT 0200T and 0201T are Category III codes. Coverage varies significantly by payer. Some payers may use unlisted procedure codes (e.g., 27299) if Category III codes are not recognized.

## ICD-10 Diagnosis Codes

| ICD-10 | Description |
| --- | --- |
| M80.08XA | Age-related osteoporosis with current pathological fracture, vertebra(e), initial encounter (use for sacral insufficiency fracture) |
| M84.452A | Pathological fracture, left femur, initial encounter (use M84.58XA for sacral pathologic fracture in malignancy) |
| M84.58XA | Pathological fracture in neoplastic disease, other specified site, initial encounter |
| S32.10XA | Unspecified fracture of sacrum, initial encounter for closed fracture |
| S32.19XA | Other fracture of sacrum, initial encounter |
| M48.50XA | Collapsed vertebra, not elsewhere classified (can be used for sacral insufficiency fracture) |

## Coverage Considerations

### Medicare (CMS)

- No specific national coverage determination (NCD) for sacroplasty
- Coverage determined by local MAC policies — many MACs cover with medical necessity documentation
- Category III CPT codes (0200T/0201T) may require additional documentation
- MRI confirmation of sacral insufficiency fracture with bone marrow edema required
- Conservative therapy trial ≥6 weeks with documented failure

### Commercial Payers

- Coverage is inconsistent — many payers consider sacroplasty investigational
- Prior authorization almost universally required
- Peer-to-peer review often necessary for approval
- Pathologic fractures from malignancy have higher approval rates
- Document functional impairment, pain scores, and failed conservative therapy

### Documentation Checklist

- MRI pelvis with STIR sequences confirming sacral bone marrow edema
- Denis zone classification documented
- VAS pain score and functional impairment documented
- Conservative therapy documentation (dates, medications, PT)
- Bone density (DXA) if osteoporotic etiology
- Oncology records if pathologic fracture
- Absence of sacral nerve compression on MRI
